recipes.name: Whole Wheat, Oatmeal, and Banana Pancakes
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon vegetable oil, or as needed

steps.text: Blend oats in a blender until the texture resembles coarse flour.
Transfer oats to a bowl. Add both flours, brown sugar, milk powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; whisk until well combined.

Whisk together milk, egg, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, and vanilla in a separate bowl; stir in mashed banana. Pour egg mixture into flour mixture; stir just until moistened, then let batter stand for 5 minutes.
Lightly oil a griddle with 1 teaspoon oil and heat over medium-high heat.

Working in batches, drop batter by large spoonfuls onto the hot griddle; cook until bubbles form and the edges are dry, about 2 minutes. Flip, and cook until browned on the other side. Repeat with remaining batter.

raw_recipe.headline: Whole Wheat, Oatmeal, and Banana Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: Try this whole wheat-banana pancake recipe for light, fluffy, whole grain pancakes that will definitely get you going in the morning.

review.reviewBody: Quick tips - I omitted powdered milk, no biggie - Used all whole wheat flour (no all-purpose), still great - Blended quick oats to a flour-like texture and that worked perfectly - Rather than mashing banana, I just threw the egg, milk, banana and vanilla in the blender, mixed it all up and added it to the flour mixture, worked great. I have never been a whole wheat fan, but as I'm getting older and realize how important nutrition really can be, expecially with diabetes in the family, I am trying to just make better choices when possible and using less white flour and sugar is one of the big ones. This was my first whole wheat baking experience and I have to say they were not only much better than I thought they would be, they were FANTASTIC! I will be makng these often. Next time I may add flax seeds and/or protein power to add a little extra umph...probably won't even be able to tell

These are delicious! I used vanilla protein powder instead of the dry milk, just under 1/4c of brown sugar, and soy milk instead of cow milk. Plus, 90% organic ingredients. Because I was short on time, I mixed all the wet ingredients in the Vitamix first, then added the dry ingredients. Perfectly delicious topped with grade B maple syrup and chopped pecans or walnuts!

It is obvious these don't need any substitutions. However, I made a few. I made the whole thing in my Ninja blender which made it so easy. I omitted the powdered milk because we don't use it. I used coconut milk as we are trying to reduce our dairy consumption. I used two bananas. And they were awesome...declared better than normal pancakes. This one is definitely going into my go-to file for regular use.

I'm also opting for more healthy ingredients these days so I omitted the powdered milk, instead I used 1 cup of whole fat coconut milk and I used coconut oil instead of vegetable oil. Instead of brown sugar I used 2 Tablespoons of maple syrup. I didn't grind the oats but put them in with the coconut milk and let it set for about ten minutes then added the other wet ingredients including the mashed banana. While that was resting I mixed up the dry ingredients. I used white whole wheat flour for the flours. While they were cooking I sprinkled some frozen Maine wild blueberries on top of the batter and pushed them down in just a bit. The batter was a little too dense so I added some unsweetened whole cashew milk just enough to thin it out a bit. The result was so scrumptious! I will definitely be making these again!

One of our favorite healthy pancakes. Like others, I omit the powdered milk. To make it even easier, I first blend the oats, then add the other dry ingredients and blend again briefly. Empty it into a giant Pyrex measuring cup. Sometimes the oats stick in the blender blades, so I can scrape them out. Then put all the wet ingredients (no need to mash the banana) in the blender until smooth. Add wet on top of dry and continue as written. I always make a full recipe and freeze the leftovers with wax paper between them.
Excellent recipe! I made 3 changes - increased eggs to 2, added 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts (to up the protein) and added 1 tsp of ground cinnamon. So, so good!

I made this vegan by substituting ground flax for the egg (1 tbsp ground flax and 3 tbsp water) and omitting the powdered milk. I also used the applesauce and cinnamon variation suggested. The pancakes seemed heavy and took longer to cook than I’m used to, but were very tasty and more nutritious than the standard fare. I also sprinkled blueberries on the top of several while cooking, poking them down into the batter before flipping. Initially concerned about the family’s reaction, I was pleasantly surprised that everyone liked them and agreed the recipe was a keeper.

Definitely keeping this recipe! The only change I made was to substitute the refined flour with whole wheat pastry flour and added some cinnamon. Added blueberries to half the recipe and found that the pancakes with blueberries were better. Pancakes do tend to be thick but pressing down to flatten helps. Will make this recipe again - and will try bananas!

We loved this. I did change the recipe a bit but not much. I just didn't grind the oatmeal. I soaked it in the milk for 5 min. Or more wile I was preparing the other thins. I didn't use powdered milk (didn't have any). I added a second well ripened banana, and 1/4 cup ground flaxseed and used all whole wheat. Otherwise everything was the same. They turned out great.

Fantastic! I wanted to make Fluffy Pancakes but with a healthier kick so I just added 1/4 cup of organic vinegar to the milk and let it sit for about 5 minutes or so. I did everything else the same but added 1/4 cup chopped walnuts and some cinnamon to the mix. With the last four pancakes I added fresh organic blueberries and they were fantastic!
I added oatmeal with wet Ingredients in blender, then mixed with dry ingredients. Added 3/4 tsp. cinnamon and 1/4 tsp. nutmeg. Delicious!!
We love these.
Great recipe. I added more vanilla and banana plus cinnamon and everyone loved it!
Easy straight forward and scrumptious 😋

Such a great change from regular pancakes! And I love that they are heartier and healthier too, perfect with a little maple syrup for a fairly quick weekday breakfast the whole family loves. On weekends we have also added some chopped walnuts and banana to the maple syrup and warmed it up for an extra delicious topping. I followed another reviewer’s suggestion to blend dry ingredients together, then throw in the wet to mix bananas in well and save a little time.
Delicious! I skip the dry powder milk and added some cinnamon!

We followed the recipe except we did not have the skim milk powder and we added 1.5 bananas because that is what we wanted to use up, and we added blueberries. They were really nice. They are thicker and heartier than traditional fluffy pancakes but we were expecting that and really loved them.
I loved this recipe I omitted the white all purpose flour and doubled the whole wheat flour and I didn't have milk so I added Greek low fat yogurt. Win.

Made half the recipe for 3 people , but still used a whole egg and whole banana. I used erythritol sweetener instead of sugar . Also, as I had avocado oil and believe it to be more nutritious , used that instead of vegetable oil , and couldn’t taste a difference. They came out Nice and fluffy . Even my son who is not a whole wheat flour fan , gave me thumbs up.

I made the applesauce and cinnamon variation and they were DELICIOUS. I didn't add the dry milk powder and I added a little extra oil so that I wouldn't have to oil my nonstick pan. They were SO, SO good. I'm always looking for healthy alternative recipes and I have found a winner. I would definitely make these again!
